papers.title: Testing cosmological structure formation in a unified dark matter-energy model with a fast transition
papers.titleOriginal: Testing cosmological structure formation in a unified dark matter-energy model with a fast transition
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Unified dark matter-energy (UDM) models, a class of models in which dark matter and dark energy exist as a single cosmological fluid, are an alternative approach to Λ cold dark matter (ΛCDM). In this work we focus on a model with a fast transition between dark matter-like and dark energy-like behaviour. The epoch and rapidity of the transition are the key features to enable the formation of structure in this model. We studied its viability using cosmic microwave background and weak lensing data with nested sampling inference methods. We found that the preferred region of the parameter space is the one with early and fast transition models, where the model's ΛCDM limit also lies. Our study confirms that this UDM model is able to form cosmological structure compatible with the data used.

papers.titleOriginal: Detection and luminosity-dependent evolution of the high-energy hump in the Be/X-ray pulsar 1A 1118-61
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Accreting X-ray pulsars exhibit strong luminosity-dependent changes in their broad-band spectra. At high luminosities, their spectra are usually described by a power-law continuum with a high-energy cutoff, whereas low-luminosity observations have revealed a two-hump spectral morphology. We aim to trace the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar and to constrain the luminosity range over which the high-energy hump becomes resolved as a separate spectral feature. We combine dense and monitoring with three νstar observations of the 2026 outburst to trace the spectral evolution from łum to a low-luminosity plateau at ≃(1--3) łum in the 4--35 keV band. For each νstar and ART-XC observation, we compare single- and two-component spectral models to determine where an additional high-energy component is required. We also use the two-component model to trace the flux evolution of both components. As the source faded, a smooth single-component continuum no longer adequately described the spectrum, and a two-component model became statistically preferred. At low luminosities, the spectrum developed two resolved broad humps, peaking near ∼10 keV and ∼30--40 keV. The ART-XC monitoring constrains the luminosity range over which this two-hump morphology first emerges to L_ 4-35 ≃(3--6) and 4 , with the lower break coinciding with the emergence of the resolved high-energy hump. We discuss the evolution of the high-energy hump in the context of resonant interactions in the magnetized accretion flow. łum, below which it remains resolved. The ratio of the low-energy to high-energy component fluxes resembles a piecewise log-linear luminosity dependence, with breaks at L_ 4-35 35 erg s -1

papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Characterization
of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate
Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

papers.title: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.titleOriginal: The chemical evolution of the Large Magellanic Cloud from APOGEE abundances: A hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star formation histories (SFHs) that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution. We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $ Mg / Fe -- Fe / H $ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star formation efficiency (SFE). We selected 4933 LMC red giant branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code . The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, SFH, present-day mass partition, star formation rate (SFR), and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. OMEGA+ The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with a root mean square (RMS) residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at t_2=10.39 Gyr and with an integrated mass ratio of M_2/M_1=0.159, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centered at t=11.91 Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range. A hybrid second-infall and SFE enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.

papers.title: Synthesis and Crystal Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol C(OH)4
papers.titleOriginal:
Synthesis and Crystal
Structure of Bulk Methanetetrol
C(OH)4
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.

papers.title: Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
papers.titleOriginal: Forward model of the Gaia DR3 selection function
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The completeness of an astronomical catalogue depends on its selection function, which is a combination of the observing strategy, instrumental characteristics, and intrinsic properties of the sources being observed. This is particularly complex for Gaia, whose non-uniform scanning law and onboard prioritisation of bright sources in dense areas make its selection function vary strongly with celestial position and source brightness. We estimate the source catalogue selection function across the whole sky and over the full magnitude range, using only data from the Gaia catalogue and knowledge of the nominal scanning law as provided by the Gaia Observation Forecast Tool. 3 We developed a hierarchical Bayesian model that estimates the number of times Gaia scanned each celestial position jointly with the source detection efficiency, and fitted it via Markov chain Monte Carlo to the 1,806,196,447 sources in 3 with reported celestial positions, G magnitudes, and astrometric matched transit counts. 3 is essentially complete for G ∈ (5,19.5) in the on-sky median. After that, the completeness decreases with magnitude according to the scanning law pattern combined with the imprint of crowded regions. The completeness is also lower at the very bright end of the survey, consistent with the known limitations on Gaia observations of bright stars. We find an unexpected completeness increase beyond G ∼ 21, which we conclude is an artefact caused by extended sources, as confirmed by cross-matching against Euclid's Q1 catalogue. Our approach builds on previous efforts that use the understanding of the Gaia survey strategy to model the survey selection function. Our model does not rely on a precise knowledge of the Gaia scanning law, making it more robust, while retaining the capability of deriving an all-sky selection function without the need to extrapolate from limited external surveys providing `ground truth'. Treating the scanning law as part of the inference process, and anchoring it to all sources of all magnitudes on a fine-grained grid on the sky, removes the need for an explicit crowding correction. The resulting selection function, valid everywhere where Gaia data are available, is released as part of the GaiaUnlimited Python package. 3

papers.title: RR Lyrae stars as distance indicators. I. Sample selection and characterisation
papers.titleOriginal: RR Lyrae stars as distance indicators. I. Sample selection and characterisation
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: RR Lyrae (RRL) stars are well-established Population II distance indicators, with period–metallicity–luminosity (PLZ) relations linking pulsational properties to absolute luminosity. Gaia parallaxes now allow these relations to be anchored to geometric distances with unprecedented precision, offering an independent route to the extragalactic distance scale. We present the first paper in a series aimed at deriving new empirical PLZ and metallicity–luminosity relations for RRL in the optical and near-infrared. We describe the selection and characterisation of a sample of bright nearby field RRL, with distances anchored to reliable Gaia DR3 parallaxes. We conducted a multi-band photometric campaign of 172 RRL: 101 in Johnson–Cousins UBVRI with the IAC80 telescope and 130 in JHKs with the IRSF telescope, with 59 stars in common. The iron abundances come from the Spectroscopic Rome RRL Catalog catalogue, mostly from high-resolution spectroscopy. The light curves were modelled with GLOESS (optical) and near-infrared templates, and the mean magnitudes, amplitudes, and Fourier parameters were derived via a bootstrap Monte Carlo method. The linear relations were fitted with a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo method. The sample spans -3.4 to 0.2 dex in feh. We found tight relations between the Fourier parameter ϕ_31 in each optical and Gaia band and its V-band value for RRab stars (scatter below 0.06). The near-infrared amplitude ratios with respect to V or G increase continuously with period, without the break reported in globular clusters. We provide a homogeneous calibration of the colour at minimum light across all filter combinations from U-B to H-K_s, revealing significant period and metallicity dependences, and we use it to derive reddening estimates for 15 stars outside current 3D extinction maps. This sample and its characterisation provide the foundation for the PLZ and metallicity–luminosity calibrations to be presented in Paper II.

papers.title: AGNFormer. I: Reconstruction of active galactic nucleus spectra using a probabilistic transformer model
papers.titleOriginal: AGNFormer. I: Reconstruction of active galactic nucleus spectra using a probabilistic transformer model
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: When analysing spectroscopic data to extract physical properties, emphasis is often placed on small portions of a spectrum (e.g. ionisation diagnostic diagrams, broad Hβ or Mg ii emission lines, etc.), potentially discarding a wealth of useful information. We explore how an uncertainty-aware transformer-based architecture can leverage information embedded across the entire observed optical spectra of active galactic nuclei (AGNs), focussing on the algorithm's ability to predict unseen or masked parts of luminous AGN spectra, providing a direct probe of the learnable correlations between AGN continua and broad lines. We introduce AGNFormer -1 $; missing halves), inputting rest-frame spectral fluxes and uncertainties across the entire redshift range of the SDSS DR16 Quasar Catalogue. We evaluate the performance of the model on both full (no S/N limit) and high-quality (S/N $> 10) spectral samples using the negative-log likelihood and via comparisons with existing ̧iv and łyman reconstruction algorithms. The model successfully reconstructs unseen AGN broad lines up to an error floor of ≈2-6% of the flux at S/N ≈ 40, while the predictive power for larger unseen halves diminishes with distance from the cut-off wavelength of the input spectrum. Predictions faithfully reproduce the broad AGN spectral diversity across the entire optical and UV quasi-stellar object (QSO) main sequence parameter spaces, including both Gaussian and Lorentzian profile regimes, complexes, and narrow emission lines. The performance is found to be similar or better compared to previous spectral reconstruction algorithms. The high precision of the broad-line region reconstruction demonstrates that the method successfully aggregates information across the spectrum and highlights how the AGN continuum as well as weaker lines and complexes have the potential to assist astronomers in the extraction of the entire wealth of information embedded in AGN spectra. papers.title: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness
papers.titleOriginal: Diffusive Dynamics of Nonstabilizerness
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Symmetries shape the quantum-information dynamics of many-body systems, but their effect on nonstabilizerness, the resource complementary to entanglement, is less understood. We compute the stabilizer Renyi entropy, a measure of nonstabilizerness, in U(1)-symmetric one-dimensional random circuits. The disorder-averaged dynamics is captured by a four-replica tensor network, which we evaluate by S4-adapted infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) directly in the thermodynamic limit. Together with a hydrodynamic argument, our results identify a diffusive universality class for the late-time approach of nonstabilizerness to its random-state value, with the stabilizer Renyi entropy gap closing as 1/t. The same scaling is verified in an energy-conserving nonintegrable Ising chain. More broadly, our framework provides a hydrodynamic perspective on nonstabilizerness generation and offers insight into the design of approximate Haar-random states in Hamiltonian dynamics.

papers.title: Shock-driven evolution of a hydrogenated amorphous carbon analog: Pathways to small hydrocarbons, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and fullerenes
papers.titleOriginal: Shock-driven evolution of a hydrogenated amorphous carbon analog: Pathways to small hydrocarbons, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and fullerenes
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Hydrogenated amorphous carbon (HAC) is ubiquitous in the interstellar medium (ISM). However, the contribution of shock-processed HAC to the formation of large carbonaceous molecules, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and fullerenes, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we examined the chemical products and transformations associated with shock processing of HAC particles by investigating the gaseous volatiles and solid residues . We used polystyrene (PS) as a proxy for HAC. produced We a pressure-driven shock tube to heat PS particles to employed ∼ 4000,K. We monitored the time-dependent shock processing of PS in situ using optical emission spectroscopy. We further analyzed the gaseous products with the help of gas chromatography. We collected the solid residues and analyzed them ex situ using a variety of methods including infrared microspectroscopy, Raman microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry. molecular dynamics and chemical kinetic modeling, the experimental findings. We performed simulations which support Shock processing induces rapid heating, during which extensive dehydrogenation and fragmentation of PS occur, accompanied by the release of H_2 and small hydrocarbons. From this hot chemistry, a diversity of large molecular species, including PAHs, emerges. An H-poor solid material that contains graphitic structures is produced during cooling. The shock-induced thermal processing of HAC involves both top-down and bottom-up mechanisms that generate small hydrocarbons, PAHs, and fullerenes. The rapid destruction of HAC-like material, followed by molecular reassembly, offers a plausible explanation for the coexistence of abundant small hydrocarbons and a variety of carbonaceous dust species, including PAHs , in the ISM.

papers.title: The impact of M-dwarf stellar convection on exoplanetary atmospheric signatures. A 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulation analysis for high-resolution spectroscopy
papers.titleOriginal: The impact of M-dwarf stellar convection on exoplanetary atmospheric signatures. A 3D radiation-hydrodynamics simulation analysis for high-resolution spectroscopy
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: M-dwarf stars, as the most abundant and long-lived stellar population in the Galaxy, represent prime targets for the detection and characterization of small, temperate exoplanets; however, their complex activity and convective surfaces pose significant challenges for high-resolution spectroscopic studies aimed at identifying atmospheric habitability signatures. This work investigates the impact of stellar convection on high-resolution spectroscopy of M dwarfs, quantifies its contamination of exoplanetary atmospheric signals, and develops an integrated framework combining 3D radiative hydrodynamical (RHD) simulations, spectroscopic modeling, and transit analysis to mitigate stellar noise. We employed 3D RHD simulations of M-dwarf convection to compute synthetic spectra using state-of-the-art molecular and atomic line data and compare them with observations of GJ 3470. We modeled high-resolution transits of the Neptune-size GJ,3470,b, including center-to-limb variations (CLVs) and the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect (RME), and used principal component analysis (PCA) to de-trend stellar effects. We show the contribution of different molecular absorption features in the dense and complex spectra of M dwarfs. We calibrated the empirical velocity parameters used in 1D hydrostatic stellar models. A comparison with observations shows that current H_2O line lists remain inaccurate, with modest agreement in line strength and position within the K-band interval. During the transit of GJ,3470,b, the CLVs+RME amplitude is comparable to exoplanet signals. Principal component analysis can, in principle, de-trend these effects, but its behavior depends on the co-presence of telluric and planetary signals and the observational noise budget. While we detect the exoplanet without bias from stellar residuals, this result is limited to a narrow spectral interval and a specific orbital configuration. This study demonstrates the importance of 3D RHD simulations for modeling convection-induced spectral variability in M dwarfs and provides a framework for quantifying stellar contamination in high-resolution transit spectroscopy, supporting robust atmospheric characterization with ELT observations.

papers.title: Is Adsorbed CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
papers.titleOriginal:
Is Adsorbed
CO a Favorable Intermediate in Urea Electrochemical
Synthesis on Copper Surfaces?
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Electrochemical synthesis of urea from the co-reduction of CO2 and nitrate is limited by the sluggish C–N coupling process. On Cu surfaces, adsorbed CO (*CO), a species produced from CO2 reduction, is widely accepted as the key carbonaceous intermediate for C–N bond formation. However, a molecular-level understanding of how *CO participates in this process has not been fully obtained. Herein, we combine surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations to study the C–N coupling process on polycrystalline Cu surfaces. The *CO coverage is systematically modulated by varying the nitrate concentration and CO2/CO atmosphere and correlated with the urea synthesis performance. In contrast to the previously proposed mechanism, we reveal that (1) *CO is neither the only nor the most favorable carbonaceous intermediate for urea generation. Depending on the exposed facet of Cu, C–N coupling involving the adsorbed COOH (*COOH) or CO2 (*CO2) with NO2 (*NO2) exhibits a lower kinetic barrier; (2) excessive surface coverage of *CO is detrimental to nitrate reduction and C–N coupling by blocking the active site. This work supplements a more comprehensive picture of the C–N coupling process in the electrochemical synthesis of urea and provides guidelines for the design of Cu-based electrocatalysts.

papers.title: Charge-Transfer Dynamics in Ternary Organic Photovoltaic Materials Containing Nonfullerene Acceptors: Role of Reaction Temperature
papers.titleOriginal:
Charge-Transfer Dynamics
in Ternary Organic Photovoltaic
Materials Containing Nonfullerene Acceptors: Role of Reaction Temperature
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Ternary organic photovoltaic devices incorporating A-D-A type nonfullerene acceptors offer promising enhancements in power conversion efficiency. However, fabrication conditions can introduce impurities that disrupt molecular packing and the charge-transfer (CT) dynamics, thereby reducing performance and stability. This study investigates ultrafast CT dynamics in ternary organic photovoltaics prepared at room temperature (25 °C, ″cold″) and elevated temperature (65 °C, ″hot″) using two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy in combination with computational spectral analysis to elucidate the underlying photophysical processes. While the cold ternary blend preserves chemical purity, enabling efficient CT, the hot blend exhibits a higher level of impurities, resulting in population trapping in intramolecular CT-type/dark states. This impurity-induced trapping promotes nonradiative recombination and suppresses electron transfer pathways. These findings underscore the critical role of controlled fabrication in mitigating energy losses and optimizing ternary organic photovoltaic performance and reliability.

papers.title: Structural Evolution Accompanies Selectivity Changes during the Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 on a Vicinal Cu(310) Pre-Catalyst
papers.titleOriginal:
Structural
Evolution Accompanies Selectivity Changes
during the Electrocatalytic Reduction of CO2 on a Vicinal
Cu(310) Pre-Catalyst
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: The electrocatalytic reduction reaction of CO2 (CO2RR) on copper remains a key strategy for converting greenhouse gases into valuable chemicals, but its large-scale implementation still requires substantial advances in our fundamental understanding of the selectivity-determining properties. Historically, stepped Cu surfaces were thought to have great potential for selective hydrocarbon production during CO2RR. However, it has recently become clear that this distinct facet dependence does not hold for atomically flat Cu(100) and (111) surfaces with large terraces, which primarily yield hydrogen. The present study addresses how the crystallographic orientation and surface history influence CO2RR performance over Cu(310), a vicinal surface with an intrinsically higher density of step-edge defects. Our results show striking analogies to the nonvicinal surfaces, namely, an initially large H2 selectivity but also the formation during operation of mesoscopic imperfections that play a crucial role in the surface activation and catalytic selectivity toward hydrocarbons. More importantly, we report the deactivation mechanism of our vicinal surface upon extended CO2RR operation, which switches from hydrocarbon formation back to hydrogen. Additionally, we demonstrate how the desired hydrocarbon-product selectivity can be regenerated via in situ electrochemical oxidative treatments. Finally, substantial differences in the deactivation kinetics toward H2 evolution vs CO2RR, depending on the oxidative treatment employed, are unveiled. These findings establish a clear link between surface mesoscale morphology, oxidation dynamics, and catalytic function, highlighting the need for controlled surface/chemical state engineering in CO2RR catalysts. These insights offer practical guidance for designing more stable and efficient copper-based systems for CO2 conversion.

papers.title: Cascade Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
papers.titleOriginal:
Cascade
Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide
Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Alternating copolymers are fundamental sequence-controlled polymers, but their synthesis from two independently polymerizable monomers remains challenging because conventional methods rely on selective cross-propagation, limiting monomer combinations and structural diversity. Here, we report a two-step cascade strategy that decouples sequence control from direct alternating copolymerization. We target thiolactones and episulfides, important sulfur-containing heterocycles accessible from biobased or low-cost feedstocks. However, competing homopolymerization pathways in many thiolactone–episulfide combinations complicate their direct alternating copolymerization. In our approach, controlled thiolactone ring-opening polymerization affords well-defined polythioesters, followed by selective episulfide single-unit monomer insertion (SUMI) at every thioester linkage to yield perfectly alternating poly(thioether-thioester)s. This transformation is enabled by S-aryl thioester-mediated SUMI, wherein facile aryl thiolate departure promotes efficient single insertion while suppressing further propagation. Using inexpensive quaternary onium salts without stringent stoichiometric or reaction-time control, the method furnishes 23 new sulfur-rich alternating copolymers with molecular weights up to 157.1 kDa, tensile strengths up to 75.2 MPa, and Young’s moduli up to 2.24 GPa. This cascade route expands the accessible sequence-defined polymer space and creates new opportunities to tailor their properties and functions.

papers.title: Super-orbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.titleOriginal: Super-orbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Hercules X-1 ( is one of the most well-studied X-ray binaries that exhibits super-orbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of the super-orbital periodicity in is still under debate between counter-precessing, twisted--tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star, with no clear consensus. The fluctuations in the super-orbital periodicity in with data obtained during the 1970--1990 period have been reported to be stochastic in nature with no long-term trend. We aim to investigate the long-term trend of the super-orbital modulations in with more recent and uninterrupted data from 1995--2025 to examine the presence of features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. The main aim of this study is to test the stability of the super-orbital period using data available from sensitive all-sky instruments. We probed the variation in the super-orbital period in using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely ̊xte, and along with data available in the literature, together spanning ∼50 yr. We employed multiple timing-analysis tools to trace the long-term evolution of the super-orbital period. In the uninterrupted data of super-orbital modulation for the last 30 years, the super-orbital period in s s is decreasing at the rate of ∼ -5 10^ -5 -1 . The analysis of the diagram showed that the super-orbital period in also has variabilities at shorter time scales on top of an overall decay. Hence, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the variabilities observed in the curve. A positive correlation was found between the mean count rate and super-orbital period obtained at different linear segments of the curve. The modulation of the super-orbital period in from a few to a few tens of super-orbital cycles suggests that there is a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss the possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variabilities.

papers.title: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis
papers.titleOriginal: Multiancestry genome-wide association and integrative multiomics analyses implicate key pathways in endometriosis
papers.subject: Biology
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a painful and heterogeneous condition that affects up to one in ten women. Its genetic underpinnings remain partially unknown, and its precise disease mechanisms are yet to be elucidated. Here we report a genome-wide study of endometriosis as part of the Global Biobank Meta-analysis Initiative representing over 1 million participants (32% non-European ancestry). We detected 58 genomic regions (27 previously unreported) across diverse ancestry groups and new procedure-confirmed case identification algorithms. These include loci unique to African and admixed American populations. A search for genetically driven comorbidities revealed dozens of associations with known and previously uncharacterized risk factors. Then, within prioritized cellular contexts, we found numerous examples of gene expression affected by endometriosis status. Including further multiomic analyses, we implicated a total of 314 genes, suggesting multiple targets for therapeutic intervention. Our findings span molecular, cellular and phenotypic scales, highlighting interconnected pathways that underscore the multifaceted etiology of endometriosis.

papers.title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
papers.titleOriginal:
Supramolecular
Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation
of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. Altogether, our results establish supramolecular substrate protection as an effective strategy to regulate multistep enzymatic reaction networks.

papers.title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
papers.titleOriginal:
Accessing Alkyl Linkers
for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis
via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: The rise of macrocyclic peptides as a therapeutic modality has exposed gaps in the synthetic chemistry toolbox available for drug discovery teams to rapidly explore diverse linkers for structural optimization. In contrast to the thioether linkers common in peptide leads identified from mRNA display, all-carbon linkers are desirable for imparting solubility and stability, but existing approaches suffer from limited amino acid diversity, incompatibility with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), stereochemical loss, multistep requirements, or restricted linker placement. We report a Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization (D2AM) to install alkyl linkers via C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. This method uses pyridinium monomers derived from commercial amino acids that are stable to SPPS for the seamless synthesis of complex macrocyclic and polycyclic peptides with conservation of stereochemistry. This deaminative method is anticipated to accelerate optimization of peptide macrocycle structure in drug discovery.

papers.title: Electrothermal Mapping: A Methodology for Decoupling Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
papers.titleOriginal:
Electrothermal Mapping:
A Methodology for Decoupling
Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: Differential scanning calorimetry, fluorometry, circular dichroism, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry are routinely used to study thermal and chemical denaturation of proteins. However, these powerful methods monitor protein unfolding in bulk aqueous solutions but overlook interfacial environments, such as lipid membranes and confined crevices, where electrostatic and hydrophobic forces reshape protein conformational landscapes and dictate their function. Herein, we introduce an electrothermal methodology that uniquely probes protein conformational changes in a potential-modulated biomimetic environment. Electrochemistry at the Interface between Two Immiscible Electrolyte Solutions (ITIES) captures nonredox fingerprints of cytochrome c under heat stress, offering a unique perspective on protein behavior without relying on electron transfer reactions and revealing interfacial activity not evident in bulk solutions by conventional methods. Electrothermal mapping presents the protein thermal stability as a current–potential–temperature landscape, enabling direct comparison of the protein’s native and non-native conformational states driven by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Ultimately, our work establishes a new paradigm for predicting protein behavior under heat stress at membrane-like interfaces, with far-reaching implications for biotechnology and medicine, including drug development, enzyme engineering, and protein expression, where protein stability and crevice accessibility are critical.

papers.title: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
papers.titleOriginal: Odd-Parity Magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard Model from Topological Exciton Condensation
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Collective excitations in condensed matter can carry nontrivial topology and provide information about quantum phases beyond their ground-state properties. At the same time, the recent emergence of altermagnetism and related nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states raises the question of how unconventional magnetic symmetry is encoded in their collective excitations. Here, we uncover a continuous evolution from topological excitons to odd-parity magnons across an interaction-driven magnetic transition in the paradigmatic Haldane-Hubbard model. In the paramagnetic phase, our newly found sharp topological excitons soften and condense into a collinear Néel state, where they evolve into Goldstone magnons displaying characteristic f -wave spin splitting. The topology of these collective modes is tied to the underlying electronic topology, such that an electron bandgap closing enforces a magnon bandgap closing, changing the magnon topology. Our results establish a direct connection between topological collective excitations and nonrelativistic odd-parity spin splittings, with potential realizations in Floquet-driven materials and cold atomic gases.

papers.titleOriginal: Minding the Gap between Hard and Diffractive Structure Functions at the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: Diffraction is characterized by forward scattering and a large rapidity gap. Ordinary hard scattering also produces gapped events and presents a significant background to identification of diffractively produced events. We present a fully differential factorization of gapped hard e p scattering. We find that the unpolarized azimuthally dependent structure functions F 3 , 4 gap and the longitudinal F L gap vanish at leading power for hard scattering. Azimuthal dependence is thus a pure diffractive signature. This is borne out in Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: A more elongated and cohesive structure of asteroid Toutatis revealed by the Chang'e-2 flyby
papers.titleOriginal: A more elongated and cohesive structure of asteroid Toutatis revealed by the Chang'e-2 flyby
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: The internal strength of small asteroids controls how they survive self-gravity, rotation, and planetary encounters. Asteroid (4179) Toutatis is a key target because Chang'e-2 acquired meter-scale images during a close flyby and radar observations provide its rough global shape. We aim to fuse the Chang'e-2 optical images with the radar-derived shape model to obtain a more realistic shape of Toutatis and to infer its internal stress state and the cohesive strength required for structural stability. Treating the radar model as a global prior, we optimized a deformable shape using radial basis functions against the silhouettes of Chang'e-2 flyby images. The relative pose and scaling were optimized with the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy, and uncertainties were sampled using a Markov chain Monte Carlo approach. We then performed finite-element stress modeling under self-gravity and rotation and applied the Drucker-Prager yield criterion to calculate the critical cohesion. The resulting shape model preserves the global radar topology but is more elongated, increasing the axis ratio and the normalized moment ratios. Finite-element stress modeling shows that most of Toutatis can remain stable without cohesion, but the neck concentrates stress and requires a significant cohesive strength to prevent structural failure. Across plausible densities, the required strength is typically ∼200--400 Pa. The required neck cohesion exceeds typical loose regolith cohesion but remains well below monolithic rock strength, consistent with a compacted rubble-pile structure. The results indicate that the neck of Toutatis is a mechanically distinct zone, providing quantitative evidence of local compaction during low-velocity contact-binary assembly and its subsequent evolution.

papers.title: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.titleOriginal:
Directed Attachment
of Catalysts into the Extended
Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.subject: Chemistry
papers.abstract: We present a detailed investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticle (Pt-NP) catalysts on semiconducting polymer platforms for the light-assisted hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction─formed from a blend of donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers─exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 × 101 to 2.5 × 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates acceptor enrichment of the near-surface region as the point of Pt deposition via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the near-surface termini of “fast transport pathways” created within the PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2) blend film. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), for the lowest coverage Pt-NPs, combined with DFT modeling, suggests Pt–S interactions via the bithiophene groups in P(NDI2OD-T2) might dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger DFT-modeled 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O═C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings suggest that submicron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures, as expected, where charge creation requires well mixed domains, adjacent to domains optimized for charge transport. Photoelectrochemically deposited metals such as Pt-NPs decorate the most photoelectrochemically active near-surface regions, producing good HER efficiencies. Hierarchical assembly of such photoactive soft materials has the potential to provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen evolution.

papers.title: Fluctuation-induced bistability in the dissipative dynamics of generic cavity-matter quantum systems
papers.titleOriginal: Fluctuation-induced bistability in the dissipative dynamics of generic cavity-matter quantum systems
papers.subject: Physics
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that fluctuation-induced bistability is a robust and generic phenomenon in strongly interacting many-body systems with strong light-matter coupling. We identify a common microscopic mechanism based on resonances between photonic transitions and many-body energy scales, unifying the emergence of fluctuation-induced bistability for diverse types of matter, including interacting spins, fermions, and bosons coupled to cavity modes. We develop complementary methods to study both the steady-state properties of fluctuation-induced bistability and its dynamical formation at finite times. In particular, we introduce the dressed-state rate equation approach, which reveals rich metastable dynamics and enables the investigation of its system-size dependence. By comparing its predictions with numerically-exact tensor-network simulations, we identify signatures of fluctuation-induced bistability already in small systems on finite timescales. Our results show that fluctuation-induced bistability is not restricted to a specific statistics of the quantum matter and provide a framework for investigating its non-equilibrium dynamics across different cavity-coupled many-body quantum systems.

papers.abstract: Weak decays of charged kaons with an additional lepton-antilepton pair, K − → ℓ − ν ‾ ℓ ℓ ′ + ℓ ′ − ( K ℓ 2 ℓ ′ ), are suppressed at order $O(G_{F}^{2}\alpha_{\rm em}^{2})$ in the Standard Model (SM) and provide sensitive probes of its flavour structure, as well as independent determinations of the Cabibbo angle | V u s | . In this Letter we present the SM predictions for all four channels with ℓ , ℓ ′ = e , μ , based on the first complete lattice QCD calculation of the structure-dependent form factors reported in a companion paper [1]. Using the PDG value $|V_{us}|^{\rm PDG}=0.22431(85)$ , we obtain branching fractions with controlled uncertainties and precisions ranging from 2 % to 7 % , depending on the channel. For the three modes with published measurements, our results agree with experiment. For the K μ 2 μ mode, for which no published experimental result is available, we compare our prediction with the preliminary NA62 result, finding agreement at the 1.4 σ level. Conversely, the measured decay rates can be used together with our results to extract | V u s | from these modes. A weighted average over the two most precise channels, K μ 2 e and K μ 2 μ (the latter based on the preliminary NA62 result), yields | V u s | = 0.2283 ( 42 ) , corresponding to a 1.8 % determination. These results pave the way for using K ℓ 2 ℓ ′ decays as precision probes of the SM.

papers.titleOriginal: HCN detection in the Kreutz sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) shortly before its disruption
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Kreutz sungrazing comets are characterised by extremely small perihelion distances (q < 3.45 , R_⊙). These objects are of particular interest because their intense activity and fragmentation can expose material from deeper within the nucleus, providing unique access to their bulk chemical composition, rather than just their surface layers. The discovery of C/2026 A1 (MAPS) three months before its perihelion has offered a rare opportunity to investigate the composition and activity of a Kreutz sungrazing comet. We present the first millimetre wavelength study of this type of comet. We observed C/2026 A1 (MAPS) with the IRAM 30-m telescope from 1 to 3 April 2026 at heliocentric distances of r_h = 0.10--0.23,au. This time span covered the three days preceding its perihelion and full disintegration. We analysed the molecular emissions using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models to derive molecular production rates. We report the first HCN detection in a Kreutz sungrazer through its (3--2) transition at 265.886,GHz, enabling us to characterise the variability of its activity. We witnessed two outbursts, on 1 to 3 April. The second, occurring a day before the disintegration of C/2026 A1 (MAPS), led to the release of 0.4% to 1.2% of the total cometary mass, thereby suggesting a pre-disruption prior to entering the Roche limit region. We also obtained upper limits for HNC, CS, H_2CO, CO, OCS, and CH_3OH.

papers.title: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.titleOriginal: DUETS: Red giant asteroseismic binaries. Binary confirmation and prospects for double-seismic model inference
papers.subject: Astronomy
papers.abstract: Red giants displaying solar-like oscillations allow precise model-dependent stellar properties to be derived. Asteroseismic binaries (ABs), which are gravitationally bound systems where both stars show detectable oscillations, can provide independent constraints on the interior of two coeval stars, allowing us to model them jointly and potentially obtain constraints unavailable from either star individually. This makes ABs potential laboratories for calibrating uncertain aspects of stellar evolution theory. In this context, AB candidates (ABCs) are systems showing two oscillators, which are as of yet not confirmed as gravitationally bound. The relatively coarse spatial resolution of the mission can blend unrelated oscillators into the same light curve, and past studies have found a high incidence of chance alignments in ABCs due to this. We aim to confirm ABCs and other red giant binary candidates, as well as demonstrate the advantages of AB modelling inference in constraining stellar parameters. We obtained high-resolution spectroscopic indicators of binarity for a sample of 60 oscillating red giants that have photometric (33 stars) and/or asteroseismic (38) indications of binarity. We confirm 12 of our 60 targets as spectroscopic binaries, 8 of which are ABs as well. Cross-matching with Gaia DR3 and APOGEE DR17, we identify a further 9 likely binaries, at least 6 of which are also ABCs. We then investigated the impact of simultaneously modelling the individual oscillation modes of both oscillators of an AB. We inferred stellar properties for: one binary of extragalactic origin containing one detectable red-giant-branch (RGB) oscillator; one AB with RGB oscillators; and two ABCs with RGB oscillators. We find that the mode frequencies of the two ABCs and the confirmed AB are well described with a coeval modelling of the stellar components. We demonstrate that the simultaneous modelling of ABs with two RGB stars can be used to infer the stellar helium content down to 3% precision, compared to 5% when using only the brightest star. Finally, the metal-poor binary KIC,2971380 hints at a need to correct the ν_̊m max scaling relation, supporting recent studies of extremely metal-poor oscillators. Kepler
